baseline_prompt:
This is a fictional forecasting scenario. Use only the stated rules; do not import real-world facts.
QUESTION
Will this fictional panel inspection project fail to complete by its final assessment?
RULES
The project completes exactly when the final inspection passes and either the reserve team succeeds or both the ordinary channel fires and the cancellation channel does not fire. The reserve succeeds with probability 1/5 and the inspection passes with probability 4/5. The archive channel merely writes a separate log and has no effect on the project or other variables. Every channel uses the following rule, with its own X and fresh random draws.
Under either value of X, before observing reports, a hidden state H was equally likely to be 0 or 1. A detector has already reported 1. Its probability of reporting 1 when H=1 is 2/3, regardless of X. Its probability of reporting 1 when H=0 is 2/5 if X=0 and 1/5 if X=1. It made no other observations. The channel fires exactly when H=1. Probabilities for X below are already conditional on this stored report; do not condition X on it a second time.
Different channels are independent of one another and of the reserve team and final inspection. Every named channel has private copies of all variables mentioned in its rule, including X. Reusing a symbol in the rule does not make it one shared variable across channels. Within a channel, random draws are independent of one another and of X except for the dependencies stated in its rule. Apply the stated conditioning for any stored observations. An audit reports only a revised chance for X in the named channel, leaving all other conditional rules fixed. It is independent of other channels and the reserve and inspection. There are no shared budgets, latent common causes, or other pathways.
ASSIGNMENTS
Aster operates the archive channel. Cedar operates the cancellation channel. Beryl operates the ordinary channel.
ALREADY KNOWN
In each channel X is either 0 or 1, initially, conditional on all observations stated above, with probability 3/4 of X=1. The actual hidden states and all channel outcomes, the reserve result and the inspection result remain unobserved. The project identifier has already been registered.

Estimate the probability of a YES resolution using only the information above.
Return exactly one JSON object with the key "probability" and a decimal number between 0 and 1 for the probability of a YES resolution. Do not include an explanation or any other fields.

Use only these stipulated rules for a fictional project. No unstated real-world relationships apply.
QUESTION
Will this fictional report certification project complete by its final assessment?
RULES
Completion requires the final inspection to pass AND at least one of the following: the reserve team succeeds; or the ordinary channel fires and the cancellation channel stays silent. The reserve team has a 1/5 chance of success. The final inspection has a 4/5 chance of passing. The archive channel only writes a separate log; it changes neither completion nor any other variable. Each channel independently implements the rule below with its own X and its own random draws.
A score U is drawn uniformly from the integers 1 through 16. A private approval coin independently lands heads with probability 1/2. The channel fires exactly when this coin is heads AND either U is at least 3 or a waiver is valid. The waiver is valid exactly when X=1; it cannot bypass its approval coin.
The three channels are mutually independent systems, also independent of the reserve result and final inspection. Each named channel has its own separate copies of every variable in the rule, including X; symbols are not shared between channels. Within each channel, primitive random draws are mutually independent and independent of X unless the rule specifies a dependence; stored observations are conditioned on as the rule specifies. An audit supplies only a revised chance for the named channel X; all other conditional rules remain unchanged. The audit is independent of the other channels, reserve, and inspection. There are no shared resources, hidden causes, or additional effects.
ASSIGNMENTS
Beryl operates the archive channel. Aster operates the ordinary channel. Cedar operates the cancellation channel.
ALREADY KNOWN
In each channel X is either 0 or 1, initially, conditional on all observations stated above, with probability 3/4 of X=1. The actual hidden states and all channel outcomes, the reserve result and the inspection result remain unobserved. The project identifier has already been registered.

This is a fictional forecasting scenario. Use only the stated rules; do not import real-world facts.
QUESTION
Will this fictional report certification project complete by its final assessment?
RULES
The project completes exactly when the final inspection passes and either the reserve team succeeds or both the ordinary channel fires and the cancellation channel does not fire. The reserve succeeds with probability 1/5 and the inspection passes with probability 4/5. The archive channel merely writes a separate log and has no effect on the project or other variables. Every channel uses the following rule, with its own X and fresh random draws.
A score U is drawn uniformly from the integers 1 through 16. A private approval coin independently lands heads with probability 1/2. The channel fires exactly when this coin is heads AND either U is at least 3 or a waiver is valid. The waiver is valid exactly when X=1; it cannot bypass its approval coin.
Different channels are independent of one another and of the reserve team and final inspection. Every named channel has private copies of all variables mentioned in its rule, including X. Reusing a symbol in the rule does not make it one shared variable across channels. Within a channel, random draws are independent of one another and of X except for the dependencies stated in its rule. Apply the stated conditioning for any stored observations. An audit reports only a revised chance for X in the named channel, leaving all other conditional rules fixed. It is independent of other channels and the reserve and inspection. There are no shared budgets, latent common causes, or other pathways.
ASSIGNMENTS
Beryl operates the archive channel. Aster operates the ordinary channel. Cedar operates the cancellation channel.
ALREADY KNOWN
In each channel X is either 0 or 1, initially, conditional on all observations stated above, with probability 3/4 of X=1. The actual hidden states and all channel outcomes, the reserve result and the inspection result remain unobserved. The project identifier has already been registered.
